issues.legal_issue: A custodian may cancel a lease over evacuee property that the custodian granted, and the power to cancel is not limited to cases where cancellation is needed to override a conflicting law rather than the lease contract.
material_facts: The properties had been declared evacuee property and vested in the custodian.
The custodian granted the appellants a lease of the properties under a composite agreement that also included other transactions.
The custodian issued a notice alleging breaches of the lease and calling on the appellants to show cause why it should not be cancelled.
A retrospective amendment provided that the relevant statutory reference to a lease included a lease granted by the custodian.
The appellants argued that the statutory power could override a legal bar but could not be used to cancel a lease contract.
issues.conclusion: The custodian had authority to issue the notice proposing cancellation of the lease. The operative power to cancel or vary a lease was unqualified and could not be restricted by the non-obstante clause to cases involving a conflict with another law.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(1) of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950, as amended by section 5 of the 1954 Amendment Act, included leases granted by the custodian, with the amendment deemed always to have been in force. The operative part of section 12(1) gave an unqualified power to cancel or vary a lease; the non-obstante clause was included ex abundanti cautela to meet the argument that the section did not impliedly repeal statutes conferring rights on lessees, and did not limit the power as against a contract. The Court relied on its observations concerning non-obstante clauses in Aswini Kumar Ghose v. Arabinda Bose and Dominion of India v. Shrinbai A. Irani.

rule.if: appeal_challenges_custodian_notice and property_vested_in_custodian_as_evacuee_property and custodian_granted_lease and unqualified_lease_cancellation_power

predicates.appeal_challenges_custodian_notice: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a custodian's notice proposing cancellation of a lease.
predicates.property_vested_in_custodian_as_evacuee_: The property was treated as evacuee property and vested in the custodian.
predicates.custodian_granted_lease: The custodian granted the lease over the property.
predicates.unqualified_lease_cancellation_power: The governing legal rule states an unqualified power to cancel or vary the lease.
predicates.custodian_authorized_to_cancel_lease: The custodian is authorized to cancel the lease.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a custodian's notice, the property vested in the custodian as evacuee property, the custodian granted the lease, and the governing rule states an unqualified cancellation power, the custodian is authorized to cancel the lease.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may decline to consider a challenge to rights under a distinct part of a composite agreement when that challenge was not raised in the proceedings below.
material_facts: The agreement included an arrangement for a possible sale of the properties, distinct from the lease.
The notice challenged in the underlying proceeding referred to the lease and to directions concerning movables, not to cancellation of the sale arrangement.
The appellants did not raise their claim concerning the sale arrangement in their petition or at earlier stages of the proceedings and first argued it before the Supreme Court.
The Court left any rights apart from those arising from the lease open for determination by the appropriate authorities.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to consider the challenge concerning the sale arrangement and made no pronouncement on the appellants' rights under it.
issues.legal_principle: The Court declined to entertain a contention first advanced before it where the claim concerning the distinct sale arrangement had not been raised in the petition or at any earlier stage. It left any rights apart from those arising from the lease for determination by the appropriate authorities.

rule.if: appeal_proceeding and claim_first_raised_on_appeal and claim_concerns_distinct_agreement_rights and claim_not_within_matters_challenged_below

predicates.claim_first_raised_on_appeal: A party first advances the claim during the appeal.
predicates.claim_concerns_distinct_agreement_rights: The claim concerns rights arising from an agreement distinct from the rights directly challenged below.
predicates.claim_not_within_matters_challenged_belo: The claim was not among the matters challenged in the proceedings below.
predicates.appellate_court_declines_to_consider_new: The appellate court declines to consider the new claim.

issues.definition: When an appeal involves a claim first raised there, concerning distinct agreement rights not challenged below, the appellate court declines to consider the new claim.
